title: Prioritized region-binding with overflow damping and variant degradation controls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a prioritized region-binding policy that prefers tenant-affinitized dedicated capacity, supports controlled overflow to hosted capacity, and degrades to compatible model variants using explicit safety controls and damping to avoid oscillation.
background: Customer-facing incidents in Q1 highlighted two recurring problems: (1) aggressive spillover from Dedicated pools into Hosted endpoints creates uneven load and unpredictability of unit costs for tenants; (2) naive variant fallback (e.g., switching from quantized to FP16 or to smaller model family) led to quality regressions and cascading retries. We need an explicit policy that encodes tenant affinity, capacity scoring, damping windows, and variant compatibility with quality controls.
proposal: Introduce a three-stage routing decision: 1) Region-binding check (soft affinity to reserved region & zone), 2) Tier selection using a capacity score + tenant priority, 3) Controlled overflow to hosted via a damping-aware circuit (overflow damping window + token-budget guardrails), and 4) Variant fallback only when quality-preserving variants exist and after adaptive throttling. Add observability and test harness to verify behavior under bursts.
technical_design: - Capacity scoring: score = reserved_units_utilization * (1 + preemption_penalty) + estimated_queue_latency; lower is better. - Damping: maintain an overflow_state per tenant-region-tier with exponentially decaying counters (half-life configurable) to prevent thrashing. - Circuit: overflow allowed only if (a) capacity_score below threshold, (b) tenant SLO priority >= minimum, (c) token_budget_remaining > min_budget. - Variant matrix: canonical mapping of model families and variant compatibility labels (functional_equivalence, quality_preserving, faster_but_lower_quality). - Fallback sequence: try dedicated-compatible variants in order quality_preserving -> faster_but_lower_quality -> smaller_family (with explicit quality metric check after 50% of requests). - Enforce rollback grace period: once routed to hosted due to overflow, avoid returning to dedicated for at least T_grace unless dedicated_utilization falls below low_watermark for 3 consecutive measurement windows.
compatibility_matrix: We will maintain a comma-delimited mapping file: model_id,variant_id,compatibility_label. Initial entries: rwd/llama3-7b, rwd/llama3-7b-quant, quality_preserving; rwd/opt-13b, rwd/opt-13b-4bit, faster_but_lower_quality; rwd/star-7b, rwd/star-3b, smaller_family. This matrix will be read by the router at decision time; mismatches are rejected and generate telemetry
routing_algorithm: Pseudo steps: 1) Evaluate per-tenant region affinity and pinned_region; 2) For each candidate region: compute capacity_score; 3) Rank tiers: Dedicated (if available) -> Dedicated-queued -> Hosted-backstop; 4) If top candidate is Dedicated but capacity_score > high_threshold, consult overflow_state; 5) If overflow allowed, route to Hosted variant chosen by variant_policy; 6) Emit route_decision event with decision_reason and model_variant_id.
failure_modes: - Oscillation: frequent switches between dedicated and hosted when capacity hovers near threshold. Mitigation: damping counters and T_grace. - Silent quality regressions: variant chosen is incompatible. Mitigation: strict compatibility labels + preflight evals + fast A/B checks. - Starvation of shared hosted capacity: mitigation: per-tenant hosted token quotas and rate-limiters. - Incorrect mapping between model IDs across environments: mitigation: automated sync job with checksum validation.
metrics_and_alerts: Track: route_decisions (dedicated/hosted/variant), capacity_score histogram, overflow_state_count, percent_requests_on_hosted_by_tenant, median_latency_by_route, quality_regression_rate_by_tenant. Alerts: hosted_spill_rate > 5% of tenant commit for 10m, oscillation_rate > X/s, quality_regression_rate > 0.5% (investigate). Dashboards: per-tenant SLO, region utilization heatmap, variant-fallback success rate.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement router feature-flag behind 'overflow-damping-v1' and 'variant-matrix-v1'. 2) Unit & integration tests in staging; run chaos tests to simulate burst. 3) Canary: enable for 5 low-risk tenants (opt-in) for 48h. 4) Evaluate telemetry, tune thresholds, expand to 25 tenants for 7 days. 5) Full ramp with opt-out and 30-day review. 6) Postmortem and finish docs and runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Router produces deterministic decision_reason and model_variant_id in >99% of requests
No oscillation observed during synthetic ramp: switches per-tenant < 1/hour under steady traffic
Quality regressions measured by canary tenants are within baseline (delta < 0.2% on eval prompt-suite)
Hosted spillover stays within configured token_budget for canary tenants
All telemetry events are emitted and dashboards populate within 5 minutes
test_plan: Unit tests for score computation and overflow_state transitions
Integration tests simulating dedicated pool exhaustion and hosted overflow
Load test with 10k RPS synthetic tenants to validate damping and T_grace behavior
Canary A/B evaluation comparing outputs from primary and fallback variants using golden prompts
Chaos test: kill dedicated pool nodes to validate fallback and graceful rollback
risks: Complexity of routing rules may increase debugging time
Thresholds tuned on synthetic workloads may not generalize to real traffic patterns
Conservative damping might delay recovery to dedicated and increase hosted costs
Coordination required with billing team to ensure hosted spillover costs are chargeable or absorbed
dependencies: ENG-88333: variant registry and sync job
ENG-92740: per-tenant hosted token budgets and rate-limiter
notes: PM alignment: Priya Singh confirmed cost sensitivity thresholds for mid-market tenants.
Design review on 2026-03-05: accepted approach to damping and grace windows.
Follow-up: add explicit runbook for manual override in P0 incidents
